29.t: PLAY PRODUCTION
Some points that may help in the
preparation and production of a play for
the Inter-class Drama competitions.
1. Clarity of speech and conversational
Each_part should be well learnt by
heart and
frequently practised
speed so as to get the sounds clear and
the rhythm correct. It is very necessary
that the meaning of the words should be
clearly understood; otherwise it is impos-
sible to speak the lines intelligently.
most of the marks are given
for good
speaking, it is obvious that this point is
of great importance and that neglect in
this matter will almost certainly elimin-
ate the play from the winners' list.
Iry to keep away trom the back of
the stage when speaking your lines. It 1s
hard to be heard from this position un-
less you speak with greater volume than
you would normally use. If you feel ner-
vous, make a strong effort to speak slow-
Iy and to take deep, breaths. This may
help to calm you. In order to be able
to do this you must have learnt your
part very well.
Try to avoid long pauses between
lines; be familiar with the other parts so
that you will know your cues well. Long
pauses cause the interest of the audience
and the judge to lag.
2. Actions
All actions done on the stage dur-
ing the performance of the play should
have some definite purpose.
Moving
about without any definite reason dis-
tracts from what is being said. It is im-
portant therefore to avoid aimless shuf-

the arms or hands.
Every position of each actor should
be decided on during the rehearsals, al-

Clean and well pressed. If suitable cos-

4. Final Bow
This should always be very formal at

81.t: Our Bishop, Msgr. Lei died on the 23, July, 1974. We had lost not only a
Bishop, but a dear friend to all Christian,still more, a true friend of us - the young
Christians.
Bishop Lei was of the old generation, brought up and educated in the traditions
of the Catholic Church, but for him there was no “generation gap" no lack of under-
standing and appreciation of the needs and aspirations of the younger generation. He
therefore, devoted much of his time to young people, paying regular personal visits
to the homes of people to advise and help them in whatever way was necessary. In-
deed, he wanted to make the Church in Hongkong the kind of Church to which youths
would like to belong.
Though he has left us, he still remains present through his example.We had
a model to emulate. His prayer life, his spirit of sacrifice and service, his spirit of
faith, his simplicity of life, his spirit of poverty, his fidelity to God's call, his unqualr-
fied loyalty to the Church, this is his spiritual legacy to us. We hoped that through
profiting by his example, we might choose the way - the correct one - to follow
Christ.
As the preface of the Mass confidently states， “life is changed, not ended”
Bishop Lei has entered a new and fuller life, which is as real as the one he had left，
but endless and without Sorrow. As he shared in Christs sufterings, he now shares in
his consolations; as he shared in Christ's labour, he now shares in his reward; as he
shared in Christ's death, he now shares in his life. Christ promised that， “He who
believes in me, even if he dies, will live for ever.” So let us pray to our Lord that our
Bishop will share His everlasting happiness.
